elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 3.2 retains automatic renewal ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term") and no mutual written agreement requirement was added; the conditional automatic-renewal elements (12-month cap, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) are not all satisfied, so the excusing condition does not apply.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal term is "equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — untethered to any 12-month ceiling, so an attachment with a term exceeding 12 months yields a longer automatic renewal. Repair by inserting a twelve (12) month cap on each renewal term.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered language requires notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term"; 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred opt-out window.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered § 3.2 or § 4.1 text; the comment notes the reminder as a preferred point but does not add operative language.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the renewal clause nor the cited Charges provision contains any renewal uplift or price-adjustment mechanic — Charges are simply "specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms" — so there is no permitted increase to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered operative text reads "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — a 60-day window, at the fallback ceiling. (The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a parsing artefact; the spelled-and-numeral form "sixty (60)" is present in substance.)

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: renewal is "for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term" with no uplift language, and § 4.1 merely states Charges are specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms; no renewal price-increase right exists to cap.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single numeral change delivers a 60-day non-renewal window, and the price-uplift element is conditionally satisfied because the document grants no renewal increase right.

Preferred level fails on four elements: automatic rather than mutual-agreement renewal, no 12-month cap on the renewal term, a 60- rather than 30-day opt-out, and no Vendor reminder obligation. These are correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.

Minimality holds: the edit replaces only "ninety (90)" with "sixty (60)" and leaves the mutual notice right, the writing requirement, the term-end trigger and the renewal-duration formula verbatim; no survival tails, procedures or extra requirements were added.

Intent is preserved: the mutual (either-party) notice right, the per-Service Option Attachment structure, the term-end anchor and the Charges mechanics all survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Residual risk to flag but not a checklist defect: because each renewal tracks the previous term, any Service Option Attachment with a term longer than 12 months produces an automatic multi-year renewal, which is walk-away territory under this rule. The rationale already escalates this; if the deal team wants it closed in operative language, add "provided that no renewal term will exceed twelve (12) months".
